subject: Private Offer Pricing: SKU Syndication, Rev-share & Reseller Retention Plan
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma@stratusapps.com>
Cc: Mark Lewis <mark@cloudbroker.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private Offer pricing thoughts — SKU syndication and reseller retention

Hi Emma,

Great speaking yesterday — appreciate the transparency on StratusApps' usage profile and your reseller network. Per our conversation, I've sketched a private offer approach that keeps list prices intact in the marketplace while enabling:

- Per-region SKU syndication (map to your three primary regions: US-East, US-West, EU)
- A rev-share lane for CloudBroker (reseller) to preserve their margin without inflating end-customer pricing
- A 12-month commit with a transient discount taper (higher discount in months 1–3 while adoption ramps, then staged back toward list)

Attached is a first-pass SKU_syndication_pricing_matrix.xlsx showing proposed per-SKU list price, private-offer unit discount by region, and the rev-share split we modeled for CloudBroker. High-level ask: can procurement confirm the target net price to the business (not to the reseller) and the minimum reseller margin they expect to preserve?

If you prefer, I can loop in Laura from Pricing and Vivek on Partner Ops to run a retention uplift simulation. Happy to schedule a 30-minute sync later this week.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Grant
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SKU_syndication_pricing_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

Thanks Michael — this is exactly the direction we wanted to explore. A couple of clarifying items from procurement: 

1) Can you provide the incremental effective net cost to StratusApps by SKU after rev-share to CloudBroker? We need line-level clarity for internal approvals.
2) CloudBroker has historically wanted a minimum 18% margin on resale — is that baked into your rev-share model or treated as a pass-through?
3) Do you have a proposal for an onboarding credit (one-time) that preserves CloudBroker economics during the first 90 days?

We'd like the internal finance team to see the math before we schedule a signature call. Can you include a single sheet with the effective net price to StratusApps and the payout to CloudBroker?

Best,

StratusApps

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private Offer pricing thoughts — SKU syndication and reseller retention

Michael / Vivek — reviewed the draft and ran three scenarios in Reseller_retention_model_v1.xlsx. Key recommendations: 

1) Structure reseller payout as a percentage of list price (not net) — this stabilizes CloudBroker margin vs. fluctuating discounts and aligns incentives to sell higher-tier SKUs. For StratusApps profile we suggest: 20% of list for Basic SKUs, 15% for Standard, 12% for Premium (these %s assume current list prices and map to reseller's expected ~18% minimum after their downstream discounts).

2) Onboarding credit: one-time credit equal to 10% of month-1 expected usage (applied as a billing credit to StratusApps) with a 6-month clawback window pro-rated if net committed usage < 60% of forecast. This preserves reseller economics and reduces short-term churn risk.

3) Effective net sheet: created the "NetToCustomer_bySKU" tab with line-level math (customer gross spend, reseller payout, Redwood net, tax placeholders). I've included a small sensitivity for exchange-rate impact in EU.

Attached: Reseller_retention_model_v1.xlsx (updated), Draft_MAP_and_Terms.pdf (clean copy of reseller MAP language).

If Vivek is good with the payout structure, we can present this to Emma with a short one-pager.

—Laura
